{{Short description|French mathematician (born 1967)}}
[[File:Mireille Bousquet-Mélou à Oberwolfach 2014.jpg|thumb|Mireille Bousquet-Mélou at [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics|Oberwolfach]] in 2014.]]
'''Mireille Bousquet-Mélou''' (born 12 May 1967) is a French mathematician who specializes in [[enumerative combinatorics]] and who works as a senior researcher for the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS) at the computer science department (LaBRI) of the [[University of Bordeaux]].<ref name="cv">{{citation|title=Curriculum vitae: Mireille Bousquet-Mélou|url=http://www.labri.fr/Perso/~bousquet/cv-en.pdf|accessdate=2015-11-22}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Bousquet-Mélou was born in [[Albi]], the second daughter of two high school teachers, and grew up in [[Pau, Pyrénées-Atlantiques|Pau]] where her family moved when she was three.<ref name=interview>{{citation|title=The Art of Counting – Interview with Mireille Bousquet-Mélou|url=http://www.ems-ph.org/journals/newsletter/pdf/2017-12-106.pdf|pages=17–20|first=Juanjo|last=Rué|journal=Newsletter of the European Mathematical Society|volume=106|date=December 2017}}</ref>
She studied at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris from 1986 to 1990,<ref name=cv/> as the only woman in her entering class of mathematicians,<ref name=interview/> and earned an [[agrégation]] in mathematics in 1989,<ref name="cv"/> with [[Xavier Gérard Viennot]] as her mentor in combinatorics.<ref name=interview/> She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Bordeaux in 1991, with a dissertation on the enumeration of [[Orthogonal convex hull|orthogonally convex]] [[polyomino]]s supervised by Viennot.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=177799}}</ref> She joined CNRS as a junior researcher in 1990, and completed a [[habilitation]] at Bordeaux in 1996.<ref name="cv"/>

==Awards and honors==
Bousquet-Mélou won the bronze medal of the CNRS in 1993, and the silver medal in 2014. [[Linköping University]] gave her an honorary doctorate in 2005, and the [[French Academy of Sciences]] gave her their Charles-Louis de Saulces de Freycinet Prize in 2009.<ref name="cv"/> In 2006, she was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in the section on combinatorics.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|accessdate=2015-11-22}}.</ref>
Her presentation at the congress concerned connections between enumerative combinatorics, [[formal language]] theory, and the algebraic structure of [[generating function]]s, according to which enumeration problems whose generating functions are [[rational function]]s are often isomorphic to [[regular language]]s, and problems whose generating functions are algebraic are often isomorphic to unambiguous [[context-free language]]s.
